summary: The world's largest video platform — irreplaceable for creator personality but exposed on tutorial search intent.
moat: YouTube's moat rests on its creator monetization flywheel: 2 billion logged-in users generate ad revenue that flows back to creators, locking in a supply side no rival has replicated at scale. Its recommendation graph is trained on trillions of watch signals that encode nuanced human taste and community loyalty. However, AI-generated video and direct AI answers to how-to queries threaten the information-lookup use case that drives a significant share of non-entertainment views.

challengers.name: Sora and AI video generation
challengers.evidence: OpenAI's Sora can generate high-fidelity 60-second videos from text prompts, signaling a near-future where AI-produced content competes for views on YouTube's own platform.

challengers.name: Google AI Overviews
challengers.evidence: Google's AI Overviews answer how-to queries directly in search, reducing click-through to YouTube tutorial videos which represent a large share of non-entertainment traffic.
